data.body:
=== FIXED: the inbound-assignee oracle's PRECONDITION. Shape (b), and the reason (a) is not
available is a correction to the earlier diagnosis. Gerrit 1226 + 1227. ===

THE EARLIER DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG ABOUT WHERE THE MAPPING COMES FROM, and that is what decides the
shape. The status update said the store copy "already carries an identity mapping for the harness
admin user (legitimately, from prior Cloud syncs)". It does not. Checked directly against the
`tickets` branch the fixture archives (`git archive FETCH_HEAD` into a scratch tracker, then
scanned every event): there are exactly TWO identity tickets in the whole store —
5749-1e26-9294-4f35 "Local Validation" and 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d "Rebar Bot" — and BOTH carry
`mappings: []`. A `git grep -o '"mappings":[^]]*]'` over the entire branch returns one distinct
value: `"mappings":[]`. And the id the harness reported, 26e2-d8e3-6077-4b94, does not exist on
the branch at all. So nothing in the scrubbed copy maps any Jira user.

THE MAPPING IS MINTED DURING THE TEST, BY THE FIXTURE. `bound_dc_issue` seeds an issue and runs a
`bootstrap-strict` pass to bind it. The scratch project is created with `lead=admin` and no
`assigneeType` (`conftest.py:382-392`), so DC default-assigns new issues to the project lead — the
admin. The binding pass therefore imports that assignee, and `_apply_inbound_create`
(`apply_inbound_records.py:200-203`) mints on any inbound `fields["assignee"]`. `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH`
is off, so the ghost lives and dies in the tmp copy — which is exactly why its id is nowhere on
the branch.

THAT RULES OUT SHAPE (a) AS STATED. "A DC user the scrub genuinely leaves unmapped" is every user:
the scrub leaves them ALL unmapped. The fixture then re-mints whichever one its issue is assigned
to, and the admin is the ONE user the harness guarantees exists and is assignable
(`_dc_support.py:28-31`). Creating a second DC user would be a new leak surface (the harness has
reclaim logic for scratch projects and PATs, not users) to work around a fixture side effect.

SO: SHAPE (b). The cell now establishes its own precondition, in two steps, and the setup
assertion STAYS — it is now the check that the removal took, rather than a wish about the copy.

  1. UNASSIGN FIRST, and sync it. This is not cosmetic. Re-assigning the same user leaves the
     inbound differ nothing to report (`_assignee_matches`, `inbound_fields.py:102-128`) and the
     update-path mint at `apply_inbound_records.py:369` only runs when `"assignee" in fields`. So
     without this the pass would mint nothing and the cell would go red for a setup reason
     wearing a product reason's clothes. That unassign both works and propagates is not assumed:
     cell `09-unassign` does exactly this and is green (it is not one of run 4's two failures).
     A setup assertion confirms the local assignee cleared, and points at 09-unassign if not.
  2. REMOVE THE ONE MAPPING (`_dc_support.forget_identity_mapping`) — drain every identity
     carrying jira/'admin' from the throwaway copy, matching how the fixture's own scrub removes
     `.bridge_state*` (`conftest.py:581-583`); there is no library delete, and
     `identity._iter_identities` reads the working tree. Then assert the absence. The assertion
     fires if the removal did not take, if a second identity also carries the mapping, or if
     `resolve_mapping` ever stops being a pure read.

EVERY ORIGINAL ASSERTION SURVIVES: absent-before via read-only `resolve_mapping`; resolving-after;
`is_placeholder`; `resolve_mapping("jira-datacenter", ...) is None` so the family is asserted in
BOTH directions; and `.assignee` non-empty as its own separate statement. The registry half moved
verbatim into `_dc_support.assert_mint_registered` so the harness-free check runs THE ORACLE, not
a paraphrase of it — a paraphrase can stay red while the live cell has gone vacuous.

MUTATION VERDICT: RED, FOR THE RIGHT REASON.
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py` is now 4 cells,
all green. `test_the_oracle_goes_red_when_the_mint_is_a_no_op` neuters
`_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` to a no-op — a REACHABLE state, since that function swallows
its own failures (`apply_inbound_records.py:130-135`), which is bug 5f48's signature — and the
oracle raises:

    THE PASS MINTED NOTHING: jira/'admin' still resolves to no identity in the store copy after
    an inbound pass that carried that assignee. This is bug 5f48's silent-swallow signature — the
    mint is best-effort and swallows its own failure, so the registry is the only place it is
    observable.

The verdict is asserted on that MESSAGE, not merely on AssertionError, so an ImportError or
AttributeError cannot be mistaken for discrimination. A companion cell proves the new setup step
works on a store that HAS the mapping: removal makes `resolve_mapping` miss, and a later mint
returns a DIFFERENT id — so the before/after difference is a fresh mint, not a leftover.

NOT VERIFIABLE LOCALLY: the harness image is linux/amd64 and stalls under arm64 emulation on this
host (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:53-67`). The live confirmation is the next CI run.
